title: Build stamp slots
responsibility: Defines the embedded build stamp format and reads a filled identity without treating an empty slot as a known build.

inputs.name: buildStamp.slot
inputs.description: The stamp text the emitted code holds starts with harness-build: and is followed by exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. A server that cannot read its own files, such as a Worker, passes this slot, and buildStamp returns null for an undefined slot, a missing marker, an identity that is not exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, or an all-zero identity.

outputs.name: buildStampPattern
outputs.description: It is a global regular expression, /harness-build:[0-9a-f]{64}/g, that matches each stamp slot with 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters in emitted text, whether filled or empty (all zeros). It has no anchors, so when more than 64 hexadecimal characters follow the marker, it matches only the first 64, and its g flag keeps lastIndex between calls to test or exec.

outputs.name: sdkPackage
outputs.description: The package a console answers from is named @dafuga01/harness at version 0.1.4. Its code comment says a test keeps it equal to package.json.

outputs.name: emptyBuildStamp
outputs.description: The slot generated code holds until harness verify stamp writes the identity of the emitted files into it, consisting of harness-build: followed by 64 zeros. The function builds this string on each call, so the module holds no slot value itself.

outputs.name: buildStamp
outputs.description: The 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters that follow harness-build: in a correctly shaped slot are returned without the marker. It is null when the slot is undefined, lacks the marker, has a remainder that is not exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, or is all zeros, and an all-zero slot is the placeholder that emptyBuildStamp returns for a slot that has not been stamped yet.

outputs.name: emptyBuildStamp
